election.name: November 7, 2023 Lakewood city election
election.summary: Lakewood voters elected Wendi Strom mayor and filled one City Council seat in each of the five wards, with no incumbents on the ballot in any council race, and voted to retain two municipal judges. Jeffco Public Schools voters filled two school board seats (Districts 3 and 4). Statewide, Proposition HH (property tax changes) failed and Proposition II (keeping nicotine tax revenue for preschool) passed.
election.turnout: Jefferson County's official canvass lists 207,052 ballots cast out of 437,532 registered voters countywide (47.32%). A Lakewood-only turnout figure was not found; the mayor's race recorded 44,843 votes, plus 2,523 undervotes and 4 overvotes.

measures.short_title: Retain Presiding Municipal Judge Nicole Bozarth
measures.summary: Lakewood voters were asked whether Presiding Judge Nicole Bozarth of the Lakewood Municipal Court should stay in office. Voters chose to retain her.
Lakewood voters were asked whether Judge Kellie Eastin of the Lakewood Municipal Court should stay in office. Voters chose to retain her.

measures.short_title: Property tax changes and state revenue limit
measures.summary: This would have lowered property taxes on homes and businesses, expanded property tax relief for seniors, and paid local governments and school districts back for lost revenue using part of the state's surplus, which would have reduced TABOR refunds. It failed statewide and in Jefferson County.

measures.short_title: Keep nicotine tax revenue for preschool
measures.summary: This let the state keep about $23.65 million in cigarette, tobacco and nicotine tax revenue that came in above the 2020 Proposition EE estimate, and spend it on the state's universal preschool program, rather than lowering tax rates and refunding the money. It did not raise taxes. It passed statewide and in Jefferson County.

facts.text: Proposition HH and II vote counts above are Jefferson County totals. Statewide, Proposition HH failed with 682,667 Yes (40.7%) and 995,259 No (59.3%), and Proposition II passed with 1,130,047 Yes (67.53%) and 543,405 No (32.47%).

The state's risk-limiting audit report lists slightly lower Jefferson County Prop HH totals (82,270 Yes, 122,416 No) than the Secretary of State's final results (82,272 Yes, 122,418 No). This archive uses the Secretary of State's final numbers.
No incumbent council member ran for re-election in 2023. One seat in each of the five wards was on the ballot, and three of the five races (Wards 3, 4 and 5) had only one candidate.
The election was run by mail. Ballots went out Oct. 16-20, 2023, and had to be received by 7 p.m. on Nov. 7.

Mayor Wendi Strom and council members Glenda Sinks (Ward 1), Roger Low (Ward 3), Dave Rein (Ward 4) and Jacob LaBure (Ward 5) were sworn in on Nov. 27, 2023. Isabel Cruz (Ward 2) was not present and was to be sworn in later. They replaced outgoing two-term Mayor Adam Paul and the outgoing council members.
Strom's election as mayor left a Ward 5 council seat vacant. City Council called a special election for Jan. 30, 2024, to fill it.
Jefferson County's official canvass results for the 2023 coordinated election are dated Nov. 28, 2023.
The Jefferson County Clerk reported that after a six-month turnout campaign, 2023 turnout rose from 43% to 47%, and that Jeffco was the only Colorado county to pass 200,000 returned ballots.
The city's voter guide listed no Lakewood ballot issues or questions in 2023 other than the two judicial retention questions.

open_questions: Lakewood-only turnout (ballots cast and registered voters inside the city) was not found. Jefferson County's 2023 Election Report (https://www.jeffco.us/DocumentCenter/View/41670) could not be fetched.

Jeffco school board totals (District 3 and District 4) come from Ballotpedia. The county's official canvass PDF was readable only through page 83 of 228, which ended partway through the District 3 contest, so neither race could be checked against the county's own totals.
No Jeffco Public Schools ballot measure was found for November 2023, but the official canvass section that would list any district measures could not be read to confirm this.

No 2023 ballot measures were found for West Metro Fire Protection District, Foothills Park & Recreation District, Jefferson County, or other special districts covering Lakewood (the West Metro ballot-issue page found is for 2026). The county TABOR notice and the measure section of the official canvass were not available to confirm this.
No recount was found for any Lakewood or Jeffco Schools contest. The margins were wide, and the risk-limiting audit of the mayor's race found no discrepancies.
The jeffco.us 'Clerk and Recorder' release on the 43% to 47% turnout increase does not say which earlier election the 43% figure refers to.
The City of Lakewood's own certified results page for 2023 was not found. Results here come from Jefferson County's official canvass.
